title: A Phone Call to My Mentor Before a Hard Exam
script: Dita: [panicked] Pak Hendra, I'm sorry to call so late. My certification exam is tomorrow morning, and I'm completely panicking.
Mentor: [calmly] It's fine, Dita, don't apologize. Tell me what's making you panic exactly.
Dita: I studied for weeks, but tonight I opened my notes and suddenly nothing looks familiar anymore.
Mentor: That happens to almost everyone before a big exam. Your brain is tired, not empty.
Dita: [reassuring] What if I forget everything the moment I sit down tomorrow?
Mentor: You won't forget everything. You might forget one small detail, and your mind will still find the rest.
Dita: I never thought about it that way. I've been imagining total failure all evening.
Mentor: Fear likes to exaggerate the worst outcome. Let's talk about what you actually know well.
Dita: [thoughtful] Okay. I think I understand the main concepts. It's the small details I keep mixing up.
Mentor: That's actually a strong position. Most exams test understanding more than tiny details.
Dita: Should I keep studying tonight, or try to rest instead?
Mentor: Close your notes within the next hour. Tired studying tonight will not help you more than sleep will.
Dita: [firmly] That's honestly a relief to hear. Part of me thought I had to study until morning.
Mentor: I remember my own certification exam. I barely slept, and I performed worse because of it.
Dita: Thank you for always answering when I call, even at strange hours like this one.
Mentor: That's what mentors are for. Now go rest, and message me after the exam tomorrow.
Dita: [relieved] I will. Thank you again, Pak Hendra. I feel calmer already.
Mentor: [encouraging] Good. You've prepared more than you realize. Trust that tomorrow, and believe in your own work.
